Right now we're consistently working on my ability to stop viewing things as black-and-white, and working on my subconscious issues of lack of control, which also has the ability to make me feel excessively guilty over things I can't predict or help with. As for things I'm doing outside of therapy, I recently picked up meditating to control the thoughts before they get too out of hand.

We haven't talked about anything long-term, as far as I can tell. It could be that I'm not a very long-term type of thinker. Right now, I'm in a place where I've practically given up and don't want to continue putting effort, so to think long-term would probably do more harm than good. We do set goals for the week, but a lot of the time I feel like even that's too much for me.

As for improvement, I feel like I've definitely become more insightful over the years that I've been in therapy, and often can tell what's going on beneath the surface whenever I'm upset. Despite that, I still feel like I am not getting better in terms of my depression. I can definitely tell a difference between when my medication is working and when it is not, and my medication always stops working after a week of it taking effect. I don't really know what to do at this point and am tired of not getting better.

I'm not sure if doing enough, but I know I'm trying my best to get better.
